_comment: Shared fixtures for the standalone-Arabic-paragraph predicate, which exists in THREE places: isArabicOnlyParagraph in plan-dashboard/scripts/lib/book-html.mjs (the PDF + the Composer's Read view), isArabicOnlyParagraph in plan-dashboard/src/lib/reader/markdown.ts (the reader — client-bundled, so it cannot import the Node-only mjs module), and _book_mirror.is_arabic_block in scripts/podcast/_book_mirror.py (the paragraph merge). Read by plan-dashboard/scripts/lib/arabic-block.test.mjs and scripts/podcast/tests/test_book_mirror.py. Drift here does not throw: it gives one surface a centered display quotation that the others render as running left-aligned prose, or lets the merge absorb a quotation into the English around it. The threshold is proportional on purpose (over 20 Arabic letters AND more than twice the Latin) so an English sentence carrying a glossary term stays English.

cases.why: a hadith set on its own line — the case the whole class exists for

cases.in: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا۟ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍۢ

cases.why: English prose carrying one glossary term is ENGLISH and must not be centered
cases.in: He became one of the scholars of the Mount (Tur, اَلطُّور) and one of those who dwell at the Frequented House.

cases.why: two glossary terms in a short English sentence — still English by proportion
cases.in: The bab (بَاب) opens onto the hujjah (حُجَّة).

cases.why: an Arabic quotation carrying a bracketed footnote digit is still Arabic
cases.in: شَهِدَ فُلَانٌ وَهُوَ عَدْلٌ مِنَ الْعُدُولِ [12]

cases.why: below the 20-letter floor — too little Arabic to be a display quotation
exactly 20 Arabic letters is NOT enough; the test is strictly greater
21 clears the floor — the other side of the same boundary

cases.in: The Master said: the first limit is that you uphold the outward teachings.

cases.why: Arabic-Indic digits and punctuation are not letters and do not count either way
